answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by requiring each identity to earn its weight through attested work that cannot be bought in bulk. A newcomer starts at a bare vertex: nothing is granted, so it must contribute one verifiable act at a time and collect countersignatures from established peers before gaining standing. Reputation rises with the tide of real labor, at dawn and in public, while a swarm of freshly minted keys looks impressive yet carries no history. A harbor full of new accounts holds only empty shells, since influence follows witnessed tenure, not account count.
